intent: Self-host a SearXNG metasearch instance at searx.kuhy.duckdns.org behind the existing shared Caddy edge, configured to earn an A+ Mozilla Observatory grade while remaining 'Vanilla' (settings-only changes, no template/static edits). Publicly reachable but deliberately NOT submitted to the searx.space directory. JSON API enabled for local programmatic/MCP use.
scope: Non-goal: searx.space listing (user opted out), so 'Vanilla' is a build constraint rather than a graded outcome
Non-goal: sub-200ms search latency -- physically unachievable for a metasearch (see verification)
Does NOT add a second Caddy, a second DuckDNS updater, or hand-edit /etc/nftables.conf
changes: Both containers run network_mode: host. Docker BRIDGE networking has zero egress on this host (nftables 'chain forward { policy drop; }' is terminal at NF_INET_FORWARD regardless of Docker's legacy-iptables ACCEPTs), so a stock bridge compose cannot reach a single search engine.

GRANIAN_HOST=127.0.0.1 / GRANIAN_PORT=8090 pin the bind. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY that granian binds :: (all interfaces) by default in this image despite its own docs claiming 127.0.0.1 -- with host networking that would have LAN-exposed it. server.bind_address in settings.yml is inert (read only under __main__/Flask dev server).

Caddy snippet sets 5 security headers using the BARE header name ('set' semantics). The '>' prefix is NOT a header setter -- it adapts to {"replace":{"":[{"search_regexp":...}]}} and silently sets nothing; '+' appends and would duplicate. SearXNG sends X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy itself (its Referrer-Policy is 'no-referrer'), so 'set' is required to override rather than duplicate.
limiter.toml written explicitly: without it SearXNG logs 'missing config file' and runs with no trusted_proxies, so botdetection 429s every request including the homepage.

server.public_instance deliberately NOT set: it force-enables link_token (a browser-proof challenge no scripted client can satisfy), which makes the requested JSON API unusable. limiter and image_proxy are kept via their own keys.
botdetection pass_ip scoped to loopback ONLY, so local tools can use format=json while public traffic (real client IP via X-Forwarded-For) stays rate-limited.
start_stack does an explicit docker restart: 'compose up -d' is a no-op when only a bind-mounted config file changed, so without it every verification silently tests the previous config.
reclaim_config_ownership: the entrypoint chowns core-config to uid 977, which would make the second setup run fail with 'Permission denied'. settings.yml is 640 not 600 (600 broke the worker's read).
No cap_drop on the searxng container -- it needs DAC_OVERRIDE/FOWNER to chown and read config before dropping to uid 977. valkey keeps cap_drop: [ALL] (verified clean).

All curl-based checks send browser-shaped headers (UA + gzip Accept-Encoding + Sec-Fetch-*). Bare curl gets 429 from botdetection, so the status check previously reported a perfectly healthy instance as broken.

Engine pruning is measured, not guessed: brave/duckduckgo/startpage disabled (CAPTCHA on 100% of queries), flickr (1.0s median), pinterest (blackholed to 0.0.0.0 by this host's own /etc/hosts -- a LOCAL failure that would otherwise be misdiagnosed as a dead upstream).

verification.evidence: Both clean, no findings. bash -n syntax OK.

verification.evidence: 12 [ OK ] lines. Idempotent across 6 consecutive runs; secret_key preserved (verified c72ff7f5e187... survived re-runs).
18/18 checks OK: both containers running + loopback-only, valkey PONG, snippet present, DNS resolves, external HTTPS 200, all 5 headers exactly 1, live search 29 results.

content-security-policy=1 strict-transport-security=1 x-content-type-options=1 referrer-policy=1 permissions-policy=1. referrer-policy value is 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' (ours) overriding SearXNG's 'no-referrer', proving 'set' semantics work.

verification.command: loopback binding assertion on both containers
verification.evidence: searxng 127.0.0.1:8090, searxng-valkey 127.0.0.1:6379. Guard rejects *, 0.0.0.0 AND [::], and demands positive evidence first (fails closed).

verification.command: real search through public HTTPS with browser headers
verification.evidence: HTTP 200, 28 results in 0.90s for 'arch linux'. Post-prune: 20 results/query with unresponsive_engines=[] across 3 queries.
Loopback client -> 200 with real JSON results. Simulated public scripted client (X-Forwarded-For set, no Sec-Fetch-*) -> 429. Exactly the intended split.

verification.command: CSP compatibility audit of actual page assets
verification.evidence: All CSS/JS/img/manifest same-origin (/static/...). ZERO inline scripts (the single <script> has src= and passes config via a base64 client_settings attribute). ZERO inline style= attributes. Autocomplete is same-origin /autocompleter (200). JS bundle references zero absolute external origins. Image results use data-src="/image_proxy?url=..." (780 occurrences, same-origin lazy-load) -- external URLs appear only as encoded query params, never as fetch targets, so img-src 'self' data: is safe.

verification.evidence: POST https://observatory-api.mdn.mozilla.net/api/v2/scan?host=searx.kuhy.duckdns.org -> {"grade":"A+","score":120,"tests_passed":10,"tests_failed":0,"tests_quantity":10,"scanned_at":"2026-08-09T15:20:15Z"}. Score exactly matches the predicted 120 (100 base +10 default-src 'none' +5 frame-ancestors +5 Referrer-Policy).

verification.command: external ingress proof (ACME cert on disk)
verification.evidence: /data/caddy/certificates/acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory/searx.kuhy.duckdns.org/*.crt exists; openssl s_client shows issuer 'C=US, O=Let's Encrypt, CN=YE1', subject CN=searx.kuhy.duckdns.org, valid Aug 9 - Nov 7 2026. Stock caddy:2.8 has no DNS-provider module, so this had to be HTTP-01 -- i.e. Let's Encrypt's validator reached this host from the public internet on :80. External ingress is therefore verified, not assumed.
verification.note: This is the durable evidence; the gitea-caddy log line had already rotated away.

verification.command: no regression on the shared Caddy edge
verification.evidence: All five pre-existing sites still answer after the snippet + reload: kuhy 200, gitea 200, dice 200, kuhy-cloud 401 (its normal auth challenge), kuhy-sync 200.
docker/nftables/cronie all 'enabled'; both containers restart=unless-stopped. No systemd unit needed.

verification.result: measured, reported honestly -- NOT met for search, and not meetable
verification.evidence: Front page: median 19ms (min 18, max 157) over 10 runs via public HTTPS. SEARCH: median 486ms (min 233, max 623) over 8 distinct queries. Sub-200ms search is not achievable by any configuration -- a metasearch cannot return faster than the slowest upstream engine it queries. The ~200ms figures on searx.space measure initial (front-page) response, which IS met here.

risks: JSON API is LOCAL-ONLY by design. format=json works for processes on this host (pass_ip exempts loopback); a scripted client from anywhere else gets 429 because it cannot send Sec-Fetch-* headers. This satisfies an MCP server running on this box, but NOT one calling in from the phone or another machine. Widening it would mean adding that client's IP to pass_ip.

NOT YET VERIFIED: real browser load. The strict CSP was validated by static asset analysis, not by a rendering engine (the Chrome extension was not connected and headless chromium produced empty output on this host). A browser load + console check would close this.
NOT YET VERIFIED by the user: the phone-on-cellular acceptance test. Note this is now about user acceptance, not about whether the public path works -- see the ACME evidence in verification.

brave/duckduckgo/startpage are disabled due to CAPTCHA from this IP. If the IP's reputation changes they could be re-enabled -- re-check with the unresponsive_engines command in settings.yml's comment.

pass_ip exempts loopback from ALL botdetection. Any process on this host can query the JSON API unthrottled. Acceptable for a single-user box; would need revisiting if untrusted local services existed.
The instance is publicly reachable and will attract scrapers. The limiter mitigates but does not eliminate this.
rollback: rm ~/gitea/sites/searx.caddy && docker exec gitea-caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

Validate after rollback: the other five sites on the shared edge (gitea, kuhy, dice, cloud, sync) still answer -- the snippet is the only shared-state change, and reload_caddy removes it automatically if caddy validate fails.
rm -rf ~/searxng to drop config + the valkey volume (docker volume rm searxng_valkey-data).
